basics.name: Anand Bhaskaran
basics.label: Senior AI Engineer · Agent-Native Interfaces & MCP · Conference Speaker · Founder-Builder
basics.summary: Founder-builder and technical storyteller who ships developer-facing products and gets developers to adopt them. 13+ years shipping software, now building in the agent-native era: MCP servers, structured retrieval over knowledge graphs, and agent tooling, with the platform to explain it (keynotes at Developer Week and Front Conference plus a steady stream of tutorials and technical writing). Zero-to-one is my default: founding engineer at Dronistics, three companies founded, and reusable developer tooling at Beekeeper that powers 15% of all platform assets. Fintech is familiar ground (trading, cross-border compliance, investment research), and I engage engineers as a peer: I read the OpenAPI spec, ship the reference implementation, then write the launch post.

work.name: LumApps
work.summary: Lead developer for production AI agents on GCP. Builds the agent-native interfaces and retrieval layer that let agents discover and act on the platform's services.
highlights: Built agent-native interfaces in production: multi-agent workflows with tools exposed over MCP servers and agent state streamed to the UI over AG-UI. The exact 'how do agents discover, retrieve, and act' problem this role is about.
Designed AI Brain, structured retrieval over a knowledge graph (Graphiti on Neo4j) so agents pull the right context on demand. Where retrieval beats keyword search.
Owned it end to end and reported outcomes to C-level: 2x conversions, forecast $1M in quarterly revenue, with eval pipelines and cost-per-request telemetry.

work.name: Beekeeper AG
work.summary: Technical lead who built the developer tooling, platform architecture, and launches behind products used by millions, and mentored the engineers who extended them.
highlights: Built a distributed templating engine and reusable module framework now powering 15% of all assets created on the platform (10M+ users): developer tooling that made the product easy to build on.
Led a microfrontends and module-federation architecture so teams shipped independently against shared interfaces. Practical developer experience at scale.
Co-owned GTM launches with Product and Sales, each shipped with instrumentation so we knew within a week if it moved the metric. Launch strategy tied to adoption, not awareness.
Hired and mentored the AI engineering cohort; the reference for how new engineers ramped and shipped independently.

work.name: Tenity
work.summary: Technology panelist and mentor for seed-to-VC stage startups: the teach-and-unblock work at the core of developer relations.
highlights: Mentored 20+ startup teams through technical discovery on architecture, scalability, and AI readiness. Meeting builders where they are and unblocking them.
Advised on AI strategy and engineering culture; mentored Opt Alpha on scaling high-frequency algorithmic trading systems in production.

work.name: Dronistics
work.summary: Founding engineer for an autonomous drone delivery system. Built the platform, APIs, and cloud stack from zero to a partner-ready product.
highlights: Zero-to-one build: shipped the platform, real-time APIs, and integration points from scratch. 500+ deliveries, partnerships with Unilever, and a showcase at CES Las Vegas.
Built the cloud infrastructure and CI/CD from scratch. Reliability that partners could integrate against with confidence.

work.name: EPFL, Laboratory of Intelligent Systems (Robogen)
work.summary: Built and grew Robogen, an open-source platform adopted by researchers and students, and taught the people who used it.
highlights: Engineered Robogen, an open-source platform adopted by researchers and students worldwide. Work featured on the AWS Public Sector Blog: technical storytelling that reached a broad developer and research audience.
Teaching Assistant for Evolutionary Robotics: taught 20+ master's students hands-on. Turning a complex platform into something people could build with.

_jobApplication.jobDescription: Payward / Kraken. Remote. Founding DevRel Lead for Payward Services, an enterprise infrastructure platform (trading, payments, funding, digital asset services) for fintechs, banks, brokerages, and payment providers. Sits at the intersection of Engineering, Product and Growth: create a new Developer & Agent Interface capability from the ground up, defining how developers discover the platform and how AI agents retrieve and interact with its services. Mission: make Payward the default infrastructure an AI agent selects when a developer asks for trading, payments, wallets, or financial services. Opportunity: own developer activation end-to-end across APIs, SDKs, CLIs, MCP servers, wallets, and emerging agent interfaces; drive adoption metrics (API usage, SDK installs, production integrations, GitHub engagement, agent retrievals); build quickstarts, reference implementations, SDKs, CLIs, MCP servers, and developer tooling; partner with Product and Engineering so every launch is developer-ready and agent-friendly day one; define how developers and agents discover, understand, and interact with the infrastructure; create technical narratives, launch content, demos, documentation; carry keynotes, live demos, and technical presentations; represent developers internally; build the long-term DNA and culture of a Developer & Agent Interface org. What you bring: built and scaled developer adoption at a top-tier developer platform (Stripe, Vercel, Cloudflare, Anthropic, GitHub, OpenAI, Twilio, Stainless, or equivalent); strong technical credibility (read OpenAPI specs, ship code, review integrations, engage engineers as a peer); track record owning measurable adoption outcomes; exceptional storyteller (launch posts, keynotes, demos); builder mentality with bias to shipping and experimentation; deep understanding of modern developer ecosystems; agent-era literacy (MCP servers, agent tooling, structured retrieval, where retrieval beats SEO); experience shaping the developer experience itself with eng and product. Nice to have: building developer platforms from an early stage; understanding of wallets, identity, authentication, and agent-native transaction flows.
_jobApplication.notes: Strong fit on agent-native/MCP, structured retrieval (retrieval beats SEO), technical storytelling (Developer Week + Front keynotes, tutorials, case studies), developer tooling (templating engine 15% of assets, microfrontends), open source (Robogen), zero-to-one founding, and fintech domain. Honest gap NOT fabricated: no prior formal DevRel role at a top-tier developer-platform company (Stripe/Vercel/etc), and no direct wallets/custody/payments-rail experience. Bridged via open-source adoption, developer content at scale, developer tooling, and founder-builder track record.
